summary: Close to implementable, but the biggest gap is how a composed KB tool's BlobRefs are traced back to their originating instance, with blob integrity-check depth a close second.

questions.text: How does the host determine the originating instance of each BlobRef returned by a composed KB tool, given BlobRef carries no instance field?
questions.reason: Provenance tagging, snapshot search or an explicit instance field need different broker/wire plumbing and differ when two instances hold the same hash; ADR states the requirement ('resolution uses the originating captured instance') but no mechanism.

questions.text: How thorough is blob integrity checking at publication and on read: existence only, size match, or full re-hash against sha256?
questions.reason: Decides lock-held cost, corruption error paths and handling of right-hash/wrong-size refs; ADR only says publication checks a 'complete blob' and missing/corrupt bytes give an actionable error.

questions.text: What exact CLI/MCP output shape carries the local file path for each BlobRef, and where do unresolvable-reference diagnostics appear?
questions.reason: Field-in-ref, wrapper or side table is a consumer-visible contract needing different encoders; ADR only says a path is supplied 'alongside each reference' and forged refs are a diagnostic.

questions.text: Is snapshot reachability for a BlobRef matched on sha256 alone or on (sha256, size), and is a matching hash with a wrong size treated as forged?
questions.reason: Decides what the index stores per Available payload and which forged-reference cases are refused; ADR excludes mediaType and name from byte identity but leaves size unsettled.

questions.text: What counts as a 'changed producer' that discards the stored position: any code/build change, or only a change to the Position/payload contract?
questions.reason: Code-identity compare forces full resync and re-download on every upgrade, while contract compare needs a stored position-contract fingerprint; ADR says 'changed code/contract must never reuse an incompatible position' without defining the compare.

questions.text: On download redirects, what counts as an 'unrelated origin' for credentials, and must redirect targets stay within the plugin's declared ADR 0009 network capability?
questions.reason: Same-origin, registrable-domain or allowlist rules differ in security guarantee and whether pre-authenticated provider redirects work; ADR only says credentials are not forwarded to unrelated origins.

questions.text: If an evidence fetch --restart-sync fails or is cancelled, does the restart request persist until a restart fetch publishes, or does the next fetch reuse the old position?
questions.reason: Persisting needs a restart-pending flag committed atomically in the index; ADR says restart 'passes Nothing once' and failed fetches don't advance the position, but not whether the reset survives failure.

questions.text: Is a response Content-Type stored verbatim or normalized to lowercase bare type/subtype as BlobRef mediaType, and is a request-supplied mediaType validated?
questions.reason: mediaType is persisted in payloads and feeds connector fingerprints via nested BlobRefs, so header formatting drift could change fingerprints; ADR only gives the application/octet-stream default.

questions.text: Is blob reclamation a diff of previous versus new index references or a sweep of the blobs directory and temp files, and where do temporary downloads live?
questions.reason: A diff never collects orphans from crashes or lost expected-fetch races, a sweep must distinguish in-flight temp files; ADR says garbage is left 'for a subsequent cleanup' without naming the mechanism.

questions.text: Does the surface hand out the bare extensionless blobs/<sha256> path, or may it create a name/extension alias without violating 'no second archive'?
questions.reason: Agents may need an extension to recognise PDFs/images; ADR forbids a second archive of exported files but does not say whether an alias counts as one.
